clusters.state_of_play: A major earthquake (7.4 magnitude, strongest to hit Colombia this century, epicentre in Chocó region) has killed at least 285 people, injured more than 4,000, with approximately 400 missing. Tens of thousands of homes have been damaged, leaving many Colombians sleeping in shelters or outside. The earthquake has affected more than 100,000 people. The critical 72-hour survival window has passed but rescue teams continue digging, with a survivor found nearly four days after the quake. Rescuers are calling for silence around rubble sites to listen for survivors. Firefighters rescued a trapped dog from the rubble. Colombia has declared three days of national mourning. Tons of aid from regional partners have begun arriving. Rescue operations continue in Cali, Pereira, and the Chocó region; a woman was pulled alive from a collapsed hotel in Pereira after 36 hours. The US Fairfax County Urban Search and Rescue Team has deployed a 10-person contingent. Mexican volunteer group Topos Azteca has arrived in Colombia to assist, but Colombia separately rejected Mexico's military rescue team — Mexico said its military rescuers were refused entry, while Colombia denies politics played a role. Hospitals in Cali sustained damage, forcing medical staff to prioritize critical patients. Civilian databases still estimate ~4,000 missing versus the official figure of ~400. Conspiracy theories falsely blaming an Alaska research program for the earthquake have spread on social media. Colombia is now grappling with the rebuilding phase.

Experts warn Britain's railways are woefully behind in adapting to extreme weather. Southern Railway cancelled services until 10pm. British Transport Police, air ambulance, and rail crash investigators attended the scene. Wildfires are also spreading across Europe, with 500 people evacuated in southwest France. Across Europe more broadly, another day of near-record heat struck on Friday, though temperatures are expected to retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.

clusters.state_of_play: Summer 2026 is on course to be the UK's hottest on record, surpassing a record set in 2025. Over 10,000 homes are without water, reservoirs are drying up, a ghost village has emerged, wildfires are burning homes, and last month's wildfire tally broke records. In Stourbridge, West Midlands, wildfires have hospitalised three firefighters and a child, with PM Andy Burnham saying he is in touch with local leaders including West Midlands Mayor Richard Parker. London bus drivers have gone on strike amid the extreme heat. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has chaired an emergency Cobra committee meeting in response. A passenger train carrying 150 passengers has derailed near Lewes in East Sussex on what was the UK's fifth hottest day ever, injuring at least 18 people, two seriously; rails are believed to have buckled in the extreme heat. Experts warn Britain's railways are woefully behind in adapting to extreme weather. Southern Railway cancelled services until 10pm. British Transport Police, air ambulance, and rail crash investigators attended the scene. Wildfires are also spreading across Europe, with 500 people evacuated in southwest France. Across Europe more broadly, another day of near-record heat struck on Friday, though temperatures are expected to retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.
